source.title: Open problems concerning the Hőlder continuity of the direction of vorticity for the Navier-Stokes equations.

accepted.question_text: Let u be a Leray-Hopf weak solution of the three-dimensional evolution Navier-Stokes equations in the whole space R^3 on the time interval (0,T), and let its vorticity be ω = ∇×u. For θ(x,y,t) equal to the angle between ω(x,t) and ω(y,t), assume the direction of vorticity is β-Hölder in the sense that sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c|x-y|^β on R^3×R^3×(0,T) for some β < 1/2. Must u have additional space-time integrability: do there exist exponents s and q such that u belongs to L^s(0,T; L^q(R^3)) and λ(s,q) = 2/s + 3/q < 3/2?
accepted.context_brief: Navier-Stokes velocity integrability from vorticity-direction Hölder regularity

accepted.question_text: Let u be a Leray-Hopf weak solution of the three-dimensional evolution Navier-Stokes equations in R^3 on (0,T), with vorticity ω = ∇×u and vorticity-direction angle θ(x,y,t). If the direction of vorticity satisfies the β-Hölder condition sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c|x-y|^β for some β < 1/2, can one prove a finite-time vorticity integrability improvement, namely that ω belongs to L^2(0,T; L^r(R^3)) for some exponent r > 2?
